column1: # address regions: 2026-11-03, in its first 15 s in nnMain the game's regions reach alias +17.45 GB, within the profile's 64.00 GB alias region (what it takes later in play is not measured here) (rewrite b2488f3b2b14)
# Unreal's texture streamer writes each streamed mip level straight into the texture's storage, in CPU_UNCACHED pools that need no flush, after the texture is
# created; without both keys the stage walls were random-colour block mosaics (found on 1.1.2, as DRAGON BALL Z: KAKAROT). Frame rate: the game's own FixedFrameRate=60, present interval 1
# The game sets NVN's near = 0 depth mode, so the pipeline bases made before it runs (the app's offline archive) take the main0_z vertex entries;
# without this key they were made for near=-w and no draw found them (the log's "pipeline archive bundled with the app: made for ... depth near=-w").
# The application pool reported under a preset (ue_quality.tsv): Unreal's allocator budgets against it, and the Switch's 3.21 GB does not fit 4K targets (docs/agents/07-quality.md)
